source_prompt: Classic Greek moussaka with layered eggplant, spiced lamb ragu, and a rich béchamel. Bake until the top is deep golden. 4 servings.
name: Classic Greek Moussaka

ingredients.name: Lamb, New Zealand, imported, heart, raw

instructions: 1. **Prepare the Eggplant:** Slice 800g of eggplant lengthwise into 1cm thick slices. Lay the slices on a baking sheet, sprinkle with salt, and let them sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. This will help reduce bitterness. Rinse and pat dry before cooking.
2. **Preheat the Oven:** Preheat your oven to 190°C (375°F).

3. **Cook the Eggplant:** Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, add a drizzle of olive oil, and sear the eggplant slices in batches for about 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown. Set aside.

4. **Make the Lamb Ragu:** In the same skillet, add 500g of ground lamb and 200g of finely chopped onions. Sauté over medium heat for about 5-7 minutes until the meat is browned and the onions are translucent. Stir in 15g of minced garlic and cook for an additional minute until fragrant.

5. **Add Tomatoes and Spices:** To the browned lamb, add 400g of crushed canned tomatoes, 2g of ground cinnamon, 5g of fresh thyme, and 1 bay leaf. Season the mixture generously with 5g of salt and some black pepper (if available). Let it simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens slightly.

6. **Prepare the Béchamel Sauce:** In a pot, melt 50g of salted butter over medium heat. Once melted, whisk in 50g of flour to create a roux, stirring for about 2-3 minutes until it turns a light golden color. Gradually whisk in 400ml of milk, continuing to stir until the sauce thickens (about 5-7 minutes). Stir in 200g of ricotta cheese and season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.

7. **Assemble the Moussaka:** In a greased baking dish, layer half of the eggplant slices at the bottom, followed by half of the lamb ragu. Repeat with the remaining eggplant and lamb. Finally, pour the béchamel sauce over the top, spreading it evenly.
8. **Add Cheese Topping:** Sprinkle 100g of grated hard parmesan cheese over the béchamel sauce.
9. **Bake:** Place the assembled moussaka in the preheated oven and bake for 45-50 minutes or until the top is deep golden brown and bubbling.
10. **Rest and Serve:** Allow the moussaka to rest for at least 30 minutes before slicing. This will help the layers set. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving, if desired. Enjoy!

source_prompt: Italian spaghetti aglio e olio with golden-fried garlic, dried chili, parsley, and a touch of pasta water for emulsion. 20-minute weeknight.
name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio with Golden Garlic and Parsley

ingredients.name: Sauce, pesto, MEZZETTA, NAPA VALLEY BISTRO, basil pesto, ready-to-serve

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over medium-high heat. Add 200g of spaghetti and cook until al dente, about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Meanwhile, finely slice 30g of garlic. In a large skillet, heat 60g of olive oil over medium heat until shimmering, about 1-2 minutes.
Add the sliced garlic to the skillet and sauté, stirring frequently, until golden brown and fragrant, about 2-3 minutes. Be careful not to burn the garlic – it should be golden, not black!
Once the garlic is golden, stir in 5g of garlic powder and 2g of paprika, cooking for another 30 seconds to bloom the spices, releasing their aroma.
Reduce the heat to low. Add about 50g of reserved pasta water to the skillet. This will help create an emulsifying sauce with the oil and garlic.
Add the al dente spaghetti directly from the pot into the skillet with the garlic oil. Toss to coat the pasta evenly in the sauce.
Mix in 15g of finely chopped fresh parsley and season with 5g of salt and 2g of black pepper. Toss everything together well to combine and heat through, about 1-2 minutes.
Taste for seasoning, adding more salt or pepper as needed. If the pasta seems dry, add a little more pasta water, one tablespoon at a time, until you achieve the desired consistency.
Serve the spaghetti warm, garnished with additional parsley and a drizzle of olive oil if desired. Enjoy your simple yet flavorful meal!

source_prompt: Lebanese chicken shawarma bowls: spice-marinated chicken thigh, lemony hummus, fresh tabbouleh, pickled turnip, and warm pita.
name: Lebanese Chicken Shawarma Bowls
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the ground chicken with cumin, paprika, minced garlic (10g), salt (1g), and black pepper (2g). Mix thoroughly until well combined, ensuring spices are evenly distributed.
Cover the bowl and let the chicken marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

While the chicken marinates, prepare the hummus by combining 200g of commercial hummus with the juice of half a lemon (about 30g). Stir until smooth and adjust seasoning with salt to taste if necessary.

Next, prepare the tabbouleh by finely chopping 50g of fresh parsley and 50g of raw onions. In a bowl, mix the parsley and onions with diced cucumber (100g) and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice (from the remaining half lemon). Season with salt (1g) and set aside.
For the pickled turnips, slice 100g of raw turnips into thin strips. Place them in a small bowl, drizzle with lemon juice (about 15g), and add a pinch of salt (1g). Let them sit until ready to serve.

Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add 20g of chicken fat (or substitute olive oil if not available) and let it melt. Once hot, add the marinated chicken in a single layer and cook for about 5-6 minutes until golden brown and cooked through, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
While the chicken cooks, warm the whole-wheat pita bread in an oven or a dry skillet for 1-2 minutes on each side until soft and pliable.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it from the heat and let it rest for a few minutes before slicing it into strips for serving.
To plate, spread a generous dollop of lemony hummus on each bowl, add a portion of the chicken, and top with fresh tabbouleh and pickled turnips. Finally, serve with warm pita on the side.
Garnish with fresh thyme (about 5g) for an aromatic finish.

source_prompt: Greek lemon-oregano chicken souvlaki on skewers, served with cooling tzatziki, warm pita, and a sharp Horiatiki salad with feta.
name: Zesty Greek Lemon-Oregano Chicken Souvlaki with Tzatziki and Horiatiki Salad

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: 1. **Marinate the Chicken:** In a bowl, combine the **chicken breast** (500g) with **lemon juice** (60g), **dried oregano** (10g), **salt** (4g), **black pepper** (2g), and **minced garlic** (15g). Toss well and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature; this will infuse the chicken with wonderful citrusy and herbal aromas.

2. **Prepare the Tzatziki:** While the chicken is marinating, peel and grate the **cucumber** (200g). Using a clean cloth, squeeze out excess moisture. In a bowl, combine the grated cucumber, **yogurt** (200g), a dash of **red wine vinegar** (30g), and a pinch of **salt**. Mix well and set aside in the refrigerator to chill; it should be cool and refreshing.
3. **Preheat Grill:** Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat (about 200°C). Ensure it’s hot so that the chicken will sear nicely.

4. **Skewering Chicken:** Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers, packing them tightly but not overcrowding, to allow even cooking. If using wooden skewers, soak them in water beforehand to prevent burning.

5. **Grilling Chicken:** Place the chicken skewers on the grill. Sear for about **4-5 minutes** on each side until they are golden brown and have grill marks. The internal temperature should reach 75°C, and the chicken should be tender with a juicy texture.

6. **Prepare the Horiatiki Salad:** While the chicken is grilling, chop **onion** (100g), and crumble the **feta cheese** (100g). In a bowl, combine diced **tomatoes** (200g, if available), sliced **bell peppers** (substitute with serrano or sweet pepper for a similar flavor; 100g), **black olives** (100g), and the chopped onion. Drizzle with olive oil, crumbled feta, and a splash of red wine vinegar, mixing gently.
7. **Warm the Pita:** In the last few minutes of grilling, place the **whole-wheat pita** (200g) on the side of the grill. Heat for about **1-2 minutes** on each side until warmed through and soft.

8. **Assemble the Dish:** Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes. Serve the skewers with tzatziki, warm pita, and the refreshing Horiatiki salad on the side. Garnish with extra oregano if desired, and enjoy the combination of flavors.

source_prompt: Spanish tortilla española with thinly sliced potato, slow-caramelised onion, and roasted red pepper. Serve room-temperature wedges with crusty bread.
name: Spanish Tortilla Española with Caramelized Onions and Roasted Red Peppers

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil
Fish, herring eggs, Pacific, dry (Alaska Native)

instructions: Peel and thinly slice the potatoes (about 1-2 mm thick). You should have around 500g of potatoes.

In a large skillet, heat 50ml of olive oil over medium heat. Add the sliced potatoes. Sauté gently for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally until they are tender and slightly golden. They should feel soft but not falling apart.

Meanwhile, thinly slice the onions. In another pan with 25ml of olive oil, sauté the onions over medium-low heat for about 15-20 minutes, stirring frequently until they are a deep golden brown and caramelized. Add a pinch of salt to enhance sweetness.
Once the potatoes are cooked, drain them to remove excess oil and combine them with the caramelized onions in a large bowl.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the eggs, salted to taste (about 5g salt) and a dash of black pepper (about 1g). Mix in the vinegar, paprika, chopped parsley, and thyme. Feel free to add additional spices if desired.
Carefully fold the potatoes and onions into the egg mixture ensuring even coating - do not mash.
Wipe the same skillet clean and add a touch more olive oil to coat the bottom. Heat over medium heat until shimmering. Pour in the potato, onion, and egg mixture, spreading it into an even layer.
Cook for about 6-8 minutes until the edges start to set, gently shaking the pan to prevent sticking. You can cover with a lid to help cook the top.

To flip, place a large plate over the skillet and invert the tortilla onto the plate. Slide it back into the skillet to cook the other side for an additional 5-6 minutes until fully set. The tortilla should be golden brown on both sides.

Once done, transfer to a serving plate and allow to rest at room temperature for at least 20 minutes before slicing into wedges. Serve with crusty bread along with your choice of savory condiments. Enjoy!

source_prompt: Sicilian pasta alla Norma with melt-soft fried eggplant, garlic-tomato sauce, fresh basil, and shaved ricotta salata.
name: Sicilian Pasta alla Norma with Melt-Soft Fried Eggplant

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: **Prepare Eggplant:** Slice the eggplant into 1 cm thick rounds. Sprinkle with salt and let sit for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse and pat dry with paper towels.

**Fry Eggplant:** In a large skillet, heat 30g of olive oil over medium heat. Add the eggplant slices in batches, frying for 3-5 minutes per side until golden brown and tender. Remove and place on a paper towel to drain excess oil.

**Sauté Aromatics:** In the same skillet, add 15g of butter. Once melted, add 100g of chopped onion and 10g of minced garlic, cooking over medium heat for about 5 minutes until fragrant and translucent.
**Add Tomatoes:** Pour in 400g of crushed canned tomatoes and 50g of sun-dried tomatoes. Stir to combine and let simmer for 10 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly.

**Season the Sauce:** After simmering, season the sauce with salt (about 5g), black pepper (3g), a hint of red pepper flakes (3g), and fresh basil (10g, chopped). Stir well and taste; adjust seasoning as necessary.

**Cook the Pasta:** In a large pot, bring salted water to a boil. Add 250g of dry enriched pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the pasta.
**Combine Pasta and Sauce:** Add the drained pasta into the skillet with the tomato sauce. Toss gently, adding reserved pasta water (a little at a time) to create your desired sauce consistency.
**Add Fried Eggplant:** Fold in the fried eggplant slices gently, allowing them to mix without breaking apart.
**Finish with Fresh Basil:** Turn off the heat and add the remaining chopped basil on top of the pasta. Toss lightly to combine and infuse the fresh aroma.
**Serve:** Plate the pasta and garnish with shaved ricotta salata for a creamy finish. Serve immediately while hot and enjoy the delightful Sicilian flavors.

source_prompt: Turkish menemen: soft scrambled eggs folded through a slow-cooked tomato-and-green-pepper base, finished with crumbled feta and warm bread.
name: Savory Turkish Menemen with Feta

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: Heat a medium skillet over medium heat and add the oil. After about 1 minute, the oil should shimmer and be ready for the next step.
Add the chopped onion (100g) to the skillet, stirring occasionally for 4-5 minutes until soft and translucent, releasing a sweet aroma.
Stir in minced garlic (15g) and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant but not browned, an indicator of a well-cooked base.
Next, add diced sweet green peppers (150g) to the pan, sautéing for an additional 3-4 minutes until they soften and brighten in color.
Pour in canned crushed tomatoes (400g), stirring well to combine. Season with a pinch of salt (5g), cumin (2g), and paprika (2g).
Increase heat to medium-high and simmer for about 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the sauce to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, crack the frozen scrambled egg mixture (300g) into a bowl and whisk gently to combine the yolks and whites together.
Create a well in the tomato mixture, reduce heat to medium-low, and pour in the eggs, stirring gently to incorporate them.
Cook for 4-5 minutes, folding the eggs into the tomato mixture, until they are softly scrambled and slightly runny, maintaining a creamy texture.
Remove from heat and gently fold in crumbled feta cheese (100g) until slightly melted and incorporated, adding richness and tang.
Finally, finish with a sprinkle of fresh parsley (10g) for a burst of color and fresh flavor. Serve immediately with warm crusty bread.

source_prompt: Classic Swedish meatballs (köttbullar) in a silky cream gravy, with buttery mashed potatoes, pickled cucumber and lingonberry sauce.
name: Classic Swedish Meatballs with Creamy Gravy and Mashed Potatoes
instructions: In a large bowl, combine 250g ground beef with 150g pork sausage. Season with 5g each salt and black pepper. Mix well until incorporated.
Finely chop 100g onion and add to the meat mixture. Next, tear 50g of white bread into small pieces and mix in, adding a splash of beef broth (about 50ml) to moisten, if necessary.
Shape the meat mixture into small balls, about 2.5cm in diameter, for even cooking.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat and melt 50g butter until foamy. Add the meatballs and sear for 4-5 minutes until browned and cooked through, turning to cook evenly on all sides.
Once meatballs are cooked, remove them from the skillet and set aside, keeping them warm.

In the same skillet, add another 50g of butter and allow it to melt, then sprinkle in 2 tablespoons of flour (not listed but a staple), stirring to create a roux. Cook for about 1-2 minutes until lightly browned.

Slowly whisk in 500ml of beef broth and 150g of cream, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Add the meatballs back into the gravy and let them simmer gently for another 5 minutes, allowing them to absorb the flavors of the sauce.
Meanwhile, peel and chop 600g of potatoes. Boil them in salted water until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain and return to the pot.
Mash the potatoes with 50g butter, and season with salt and white pepper to taste, ensuring a creamy consistency.

For the side salad: slice 100g cucumber and serve with 100g sour cucumber pickles as a refreshing topping alongside the meatballs. Serve everything hot, drizzling some of the creamy gravy over the meatballs and potatoes.

source_prompt: Norwegian pan-seared salmon with browned butter, dill, lemon, and steamed new potatoes. Skin crisp; flesh just-cooked.
name: Crispy Skin Norwegian Salmon with Lemon-Dill Butter and Steamed New Potatoes
instructions: 1. **Prepare the Potatoes:** Begin by washing and scrub the new potatoes thoroughly under cold water. If the potatoes are large, cut them in half for even cooking. Place them in a pot of salted cold water, enough to cover them by about an inch. Season the water generously with salt (about 1 tablespoon) to enhance the flavor during boiling. Set the pot over high heat.

2. **Boil the Potatoes:** Bring the water to a boil. Once boiling, reduce to medium and simmer for about 15-20 minutes until the potatoes are fork-tender, but still firm. You want them to retain their shape. The aroma of cooked potatoes should fill your kitchen by now.

3. **Prep the Salmon:** While the potatoes cook, pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels and season both sides generously with kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper (about 1-2 grams). This will enhance the flavor of the fish. Set aside for about 10 minutes.

4. **Heat the Pan:** In a large skillet, preferably cast iron or non-stick, add 1 tablespoon of olive oil and place it over medium-high heat. Allow the oil to heat until it shimmers and is nearly smoking. You should be able to see ripples in the oil. This is crucial for achieving that crispy skin.

5. **Sear the Salmon:** Carefully place the salmon fillets skin-side down in the skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes without moving them, until the skin is crispy and releases easily from the pan. You should hear a satisfying sizzle as they cook. If the skin sticks, give it more time.

6. **Flip and Cook:** Once the skin is nice and crispy, flip the fillets over using a spatula. Lower the heat to medium and cook for another 2-4 minutes until the salmon is just cooked through and still moist in the center. A thermometer should read around 50-52°C (120-125°F) when done.

7. **Make the Lemon-Dill Butter:** In the last minute of cooking the salmon, add 60g of butter to the pan. Let it melt and foam, then stir in the juice of half a lemon and 15g of fresh dill. Allow the butter to brown slightly while constantly spooning the mixture over the salmon to baste it. The butter should look nutty and have a brown color - this is the key to flavor.

8. **Drain and Steam the Potatoes:** Once the potatoes are finished boiling, drain them well in a colander. Allow to steam for a few minutes to dry out any excess moisture. You can toss them lightly with a drizzle of olive oil, 5g of fresh dill, and a squeeze of lemon juice for freshness while still being warm.

9. **Plate the Dish:** To serve, place the salmon fillet on a plate, skin-side up to showcase the crispiness. Arrange the seasoned new potatoes beside the salmon, garnished with a sprinkle of fresh dill and a wedge of lemon on the side for extra brightness.
10. **Final Flavor Check:** Before serving, taste the potatoes and adjust seasoning, adding more salt or lemon juice if necessary. This final touch elevates the entire dish!

11. **Enjoy Your Meal:** Serve with your favorite green vegetable or salad to complete the meal and enjoy! The crispy salmon, luscious dill butter, and light potatoes should create a delightful balance.

source_prompt: Swedish toast skagen — sweet pink shrimp tossed in dill, lemon mayo, and chives, piled on butter-fried rye toast. Crown with roe.
name: Swedish Toast Skagen
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine 200g of cooked shrimp (fdc_id: 175180), 10g of freshly chopped dill (fdc_id: 172233), 15g of lemon juice (fdc_id: 167747), and 50g of mayonnaise (fdc_id: 171009). Mix gently to coat the shrimp evenly with the dressing.

Finely chop 20g of fresh chives (fdc_id: 169994) and add to the shrimp mixture. Season with salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste. Fold the mixture carefully to avoid breaking the shrimp. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and add 30g of salted butter (fdc_id: 173410). Allow the butter to melt and bubble, indicating it's ready for cooking.

While the butter is melting, slice the rye bread into thick slices (about 1.5 to 2 cm thick). Once the butter is hot, place the bread slices in the skillet, and toast for 3-4 minutes each side, until golden brown and crispy.
Once the bread is toasted, remove it from the skillet and let it rest briefly on a paper towel-lined plate to absorb any excess butter.
Now, assemble the toast. Generously mound the shrimp mixture on each slice of bread, making sure it's high and inviting. Use a spoon to distribute evenly, creating height.
On top of the shrimp mixture, delicately place about 30g of roe (fdc_id: 175132) for added flavor and visual appeal.
Garnish the toast with additional fresh dill and lemon zest, if desired, to enhance the presentation and add brightness.
Serve immediately, enjoying the combination of buttery toast, creamy shrimp, and fresh aromatic herbs.

source_prompt: Danish frikadeller — pan-fried pork-and-veal patties with creamy gravy, boiled potatoes, and braised red cabbage with apple.
name: Danish Frikadeller with Creamy Gravy, Boiled Potatoes, and Braised Red Cabbage with Apple
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine 300g of ground pork and 200g of ground veal. The mix should feel moist and slightly tacky.
Finely chop 100g of onion and crush 10g of garlic, then add them to the meat mixture. Stir to combine.

Add 50g of white flour, 2g of ground nutmeg, and 5g of black pepper to the meat mixture. Season with 7g of salt. Mix everything thoroughly with your hands until well combined and set aside to rest for 15-20 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and chop 600g of potatoes into chunks and place them in a pot. Cover with cold water, add a pinch of salt, and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Cook for 15-20 minutes or until fork-tender. Drain and keep warm.

For the braised red cabbage, thinly slice 300g of red cabbage and set aside. In a large skillet, melt 30g of salted butter over medium heat until it starts to foam. Add the cabbage and sauté for 5-7 minutes until it wilts and becomes fragrant.

Add 200g of diced apples to the cabbage, along with 20g of brown sugar and 30g of cider vinegar. Stir well and cook for an additional 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The cabbage should be tender and caramelized in color.

In a separate pan, use 40g of butter over medium heat and form the meat mixture into small patties (frikadeller), about 100g each. Sear them in the butter for 4-5 minutes on each side until golden brown and fully cooked through. Remove the patties and set aside.

In the pan from the frikadeller, pour in 80g of cream. Stir well, scraping up the fond at the bottom of the pan for flavor. Allow it to simmer for 3-5 minutes until slightly thickened. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the frikadeller with the creamy gravy on top, alongside the boiled potatoes and braised cabbage. Enjoy the rich blend of flavors!

source_prompt: Swedish creamed wild-mushroom soup with parsley, a swirl of dill cream, and crusty rye bread for dipping. Vegetarian.
name: Swedish Creamed Wild-Mushroom Soup with Dill Cream

ingredients.name: Soup, vegetable broth, ready to serve

instructions: Prepare the ingredients: Clean and roughly chop the morel and shiitake mushrooms. Finely chop the onion and garlic. Rinse and chop the parsley and dill, keeping them separate for garnish later.

In a large saucepan, melt 50g of salted butter over medium heat, allowing it to foam and bubble. Once it starts to smell nutty, add the chopped onion and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onions are soft and translucent.
Add the minced garlic to the saucepan, stir, and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes until fragrant, ensuring not to let it burn.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the chopped mushrooms (morels and shiitakes) to the saucepan. Sear the mushrooms for about 7-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they release their moisture and begin to caramelize, deepening in color.
Next, season the mushrooms with a pinch of salt and freshly cracked black pepper. Add the fresh thyme leaves and stir well to combine, allowing the flavors to bloom for about 1 minute.

Pour in 600g of vegetable broth while scraping the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon to deglaze, incorporating any browned bits. Bring the soup to a gentle simmer and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld together.

Reduce the heat to low and stir in the heavy cream. Simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, adjusting the seasoning with more salt and pepper to taste. The soup should be creamy and flavorful, with a velvety texture.
While the soup is simmering, prepare the dill cream: In a small bowl, mix the chopped dill with a small amount of sour cream, adding salt to taste. Stir until well combined and set aside.

To serve, ladle the hot mushroom soup into bowls, topping each with a swirl of the dill cream and a sprinkle of fresh parsley. The contrasting vibrant colors will enhance the visual appeal of the dish.

source_prompt: Norwegian fiskesuppe — creamy fish soup with cod, salmon, leek, carrot, and dill. Bright with lemon, finished with sour cream.
name: Norwegian Fiskesuppe: Creamy Fish Soup with Cod and Salmon
instructions: Melt 30g of salted butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add 60g of finely chopped onion and sauté for about 4-5 minutes, until they turn translucent and fragrant.
Add 10g of minced garlic and continue sautéing for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Stir in 100g of sliced leeks and 100g of diced carrots, cooking for an additional 5-7 minutes until the vegetables are softened and aromatic.
Pour in 800ml of vegetable broth and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer over medium-high heat.
Once simmering, add 200g of raw cod and 200g of raw salmon, cut into bite-sized pieces, and cook for about 5-7 minutes until the fish is cooked through and opaque.
Reduce the heat to low and stir in 100g of heavy whipping cream, mixing to combine and create a rich, creamy soup.
Squeeze the juice from 50g of lemon over the soup, and add a pinch of salt and 2g of black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Add 10g of freshly chopped dill, stirring just until combined, and remove the pot from heat.
Let the soup rest for a few minutes to allow flavors to meld before serving.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with a dollop of 100g sour cream and extra dill if desired. Enjoy your Norwegian fiskesuppe!

source_prompt: Swedish gravlax with mustard-dill sauce (hovmästarsås), thin rye, pickled cucumber, and capers — for an open sandwich plate.
name: Classic Swedish Open Sandwich with Gravlax and Mustard-Dill Sauce
instructions: **1. Prepare the Gravlax:** In a bowl, mix 75g of brown sugar, 75g of salt, and 10g of freshly cracked black pepper. This blend should give a coarse but well-mixed texture. You'll notice a nice aroma of sweetness and spice.

**2. Cure the Salmon:** Place the salmon skin-side down in a dish, then pat the salt-sugar mixture evenly over the top. Cover and refrigerate for 48 hours, turning it every 12 hours. It should become firm and slightly translucent.

**3. Prepare the Mustard-Dill Sauce:** In another bowl, mix 45g of yellow mustard, 20g of finely chopped fresh dill, and 20g of cider vinegar. Adjust seasoning with salt (to taste) and stir until well combined. The color should brighten and the aroma should reflect a fresh herby scent.

**4. Prepare the Rye Bread:** For the rye bread, combine 100g of light rye flour with enough water to make a smooth dough (approximately 80ml), stirring until a thick batter forms. Let this sit for 30 minutes to hydrate the flour.

**5. Cook the Bread:** Preheat your oven to 220°C. Spread the dough onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, shaping it into a flat round or rectangular shape. Bake for approximately 20-25 minutes until golden and firm to the touch. Allow it to cool.

**6. Pickle the Cucumber:** While the bread is baking, peel and thinly slice 100g of cucumber. In a small bowl, mix 20g of cider vinegar with 10g of brown sugar and a pinch of salt. Stir until dissolved, then toss in the cucumber slices and let them marinate for at least 30 minutes. You should smell the sweet and sour balance in the air.

**7. Slice the Gravlax:** After the curing period, remove the salmon from the fridge and rinse off the cure. Pat it dry with paper towels and slice it thinly across the grain. Each piece should glisten and have a silky texture.

**8. Assemble the Open Sandwiches:** To serve, slice the cooled rye bread into manageable pieces. Lay down slices of gravlax on each piece, then drizzle with the mustard-dill sauce. Adding some pickled cucumber slices and a few capers on top will enhance both flavor and presentation.
**9. Finish with Fresh Dill:** Garnish each prepared open sandwich with additional fresh dill if desired for aroma and visual appeal. Serve immediately for the best experience.

source_prompt: Swedish kåldolmar — cabbage rolls stuffed with beef and rice, simmered with a cream gravy, served with lingonberry and boiled potatoes.
name: Swedish Kåldolmar: Savory Cabbage Rolls with Creamy Gravy
instructions: In a large pot, bring salted water to a boil over high heat. Add the cabbage leaves and blanch for 2-3 minutes until softened. Drain and cool them under running water. Set aside.

In a medium pot, add rice and 300ml of water, bringing it to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce to low heat, cover, and simmer for 18-20 minutes until the rice is cooked. Remove from heat and fluff with a fork.
In a skillet over medium heat, melt 25g of butter. Add finely chopped onion and garlic, sautéing for 4-5 minutes until translucent and fragrant.
In a large mixing bowl, combine the cooked rice, browned onions and garlic, ground beef, salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Mix thoroughly until well combined.

Take a cabbage leaf and spoon about 70-80g of the filling onto it. Roll tightly, tucking in the sides to contain the filling. Place seam side down on a baking dish or pan. Repeat with remaining ingredients.
In the same skillet, add the remaining butter, heating over medium heat. Place the cabbage rolls seam side down and cook for about 5 minutes until lightly browned. Turn carefully to brown all sides.
Pour in the beef broth and add a bay leaf. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 30-35 minutes until the rolls are tender and the beef is cooked through.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until fork-tender, about 20 minutes. Drain and keep warm.

In a small pot, whisk the cream into the remaining cooking liquid from the cabbage rolls, simmering for 5-10 minutes until slightly thickened and creamy. Adjust seasoning as needed with salt and pepper.
To serve, plate the kåldolmar alongside boiled potatoes. Drizzle the creamy gravy over the rolls and garnish with fresh parsley. Serve with a side of preserves for a sweet contrast.

source_prompt: Norwegian fårikål — bone-in lamb and cabbage slow-braised with whole peppercorns. Few ingredients; deep, comforting flavour.
name: Norwegian Fårikål: Rustic Lamb and Cabbage Stew
instructions: Prepare the ingredients by cutting the lamb into large pieces, roughly 150g each, and season with salt and black pepper. Set it aside to marinate while you prepare the vegetables.
In a large heavy-bottom pot, melt 30g of salted butter over medium-high heat until foamy (2 minutes).

Add the seasoned lamb pieces to the pot. Sear them for about 4-5 minutes on each side or until they develop a rich golden-brown crust. This step will build fond (the browned bits) that adds depth to the dish.
Remove the lamb pieces from the pot and set aside. In the same pot, add the diced onions and carrots. Sauté for about 5 minutes until the onions are translucent and fragrant, stirring frequently.
Return the lamb to the pot and sprinkle the whole peppercorns and bay leaves over it. Move the lamb around slightly to ensure the spices coat it well, and sauté for another 2 minutes.
Add 1 liter of water to the pot, ensuring the lamb is mostly submerged. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a gentle simmer.

Cover the pot partially, and let everything cook for about 1.5 to 2 hours, stirring occasionally. The lamb should become tender and the broth should thicken slightly, filling your kitchen with savory aromas.
While the lamb cooks, chop the cabbage into quarters, removing the core. After 1.5 hours of simmering, add the cabbage to the pot.
Continue to cook uncovered for an additional 30 minutes, allowing the cabbage to soften and absorb the flavors. Taste for seasoning and adjust salt if necessary before serving.
Once fully cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Let it rest for 10 minutes before serving in large bowls with the tender lamb, cabbage, and a generous ladle of broth.

source_prompt: Indian chicken tikka masala in a rich tomato-cream sauce with garam masala, fenugreek, and ginger. Basmati rice and warm naan.
name: Creamy Tomato Chicken Tikka Masala

ingredients.name: Bread, naan, plain, commercially prepared, refrigerated

instructions: Heat 30g of mustard oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering, about 2-3 minutes.
Add 150g of finely chopped onions and sauté, stirring occasionally, for about 5-7 minutes until they become translucent and start to brown.
Add 20g of minced garlic and sauté for an additional minute until fragrant, ensuring not to burn the garlic.
Mix in 600g of ground chicken and cook, breaking it apart with a wooden spoon, for about 8-10 minutes until browned and no longer pink.
Sprinkle in 5g of fenugreek seeds, 5g of cumin, 5g of coriander, 5g of turmeric, and 3g of black pepper. Stir to bloom the spices for about 1-2 minutes until aromatic.
Pour in 400g of crushed canned tomatoes and mix well. Reduce heat to medium-low and let it simmer for 10 minutes, letting the flavors meld together.
Stir in 100g of cream cheese and mix until fully incorporated, creating a luscious, creamy sauce. Adjust seasoning with salt to taste, about 3g or more as necessary.
Let it simmer for an additional 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and is heated through.
While the sauce cooks, warm 300g of naan bread in the oven or on a skillet until soft and desirable.
Serve the Chicken Tikka Masala hot, garnished with fresh herbs if desired, alongside the warm naan.

source_prompt: Japanese chicken teriyaki rice bowls with a glossy soy-mirin glaze, steamed rice, sesame broccoli, and pickled ginger.
name: Glossy Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowls with Sesame Broccoli and Pickled Ginger

ingredients.name: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
Shortening industrial, lard and vegetable oil

instructions: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat until hot, about 2-3 minutes.
Add the vegetable oil and let it heat for about 30 seconds until shimmering.
Add the ground chicken to the skillet and use a spatula to break it apart. Cook for about 5-6 minutes until browned, stirring occasionally until golden and the chicken is cooked through.
While chicken is cooking, finely grate the ginger root and set aside.
Once the chicken is browned, reduce the heat to medium and add the soy sauce, sugar, and grated ginger to the skillet. Stir well to combine.
Cook for an additional 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the chicken in a glossy glaze, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli in a separate pot with about 1 inch of water for 4-5 minutes until bright green and tender, but still crisp.
Remove the broccoli from heat, drizzle with a touch of olive oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
To serve, place a generous scoop of the teriyaki chicken on top of a bed of rice. Add the steamed broccoli on the side and top with sliced scallions for freshness.
Finish the dish with a drizzle of cider vinegar for tang, and top with pickled ginger for a contrasting flavor. Serve immediately.

source_prompt: Indonesian nasi goreng with shrimp, kecap manis, fried shallots, prawn crackers, and a fried egg on top.
name: Indonesian Shrimp Nasi Goreng

ingredients.name: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Shortening, household, lard and vegetable oil
Sauce, peanut, made from peanut butter, water, soy sauce
Margarine-like, vegetable oil spread, 67-70% fat, tub

instructions: Prepare the ingredients by finely chopping the shallots, garlic, and onions. Cut spring onions into thin slices. Clean and devein the shrimp if they are not prepped.
In a large frying pan or wok, heat 2 tablespoons (30g) of vegetable oil over medium-high heat until shimmering (about 2 minutes). You should hear a sizzle when food is added.
Add chopped shallots and sauté for 2-3 minutes until they are translucent, stirring regularly. The aroma should be sweet and mild.
Add minced garlic (2 cloves) and continue to sauté for another minute until fragrant. Take care not to burn the garlic as it can turn bitter.
Push the shallots and garlic to the side, add the shrimp to the pan, and sear for about 3-4 minutes until they turn pink and opaque. This will develop a rich flavor from the fond.
Next, add the cooked rice (for best results, use day-old rice) to the pan and stir-fry for approximately 5 minutes until the rice is heated through and starts to slightly crisp.
Drizzle the soy sauce and kecap manis (approximately 2 tablespoons each) over the rice, stirring well to combine. At this point, you can add in red chili flakes to taste for heat.
Fold in the spring onions and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with additional soy sauce or salt as needed.
In a separate pan, heat a little oil and fry the eggs sunny-side-up or to your preference until the edges are crisp. This should take about 3 minutes on medium heat.
To serve, plate the nasi goreng, top each serving with a fried egg, a generous sprinkle of fried shallots, and a handful of shrimp crackers. Garnish with lime wedges if desired.

source_prompt: Whole-roasted cauliflower steaks with tahini-lemon sauce, ruby pomegranate seeds, toasted almonds, and parsley.
name: Whole-Roasted Cauliflower Steaks with Tahini-Lemon Sauce and Pomegranate
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). This high heat will help achieve a beautifully roasted texture.
Prepare the cauliflower by removing the leaves and cutting it into thick steaks, about 2 to 3 cm thick. You should aim for about 4-6 steaks depending on the size of the cauliflower.

Drizzle the cauliflower steaks generously with olive oil (about 30g per steak). Use your hands to rub the oil evenly across the surfaces. Season both sides with salt and freshly cracked black pepper, ensuring they are well coated. Let them sit for about 5 minutes to absorb the flavors.

In a large, oven-safe skillet, heat a tablespoon of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add the cauliflower steaks and sear for 3-4 minutes on each side until they are golden brown. You should hear a nice sizzle, and there should be a toasted aroma wafting up.

Once all sides are nicely browned, transfer the skillet to the preheated oven. Roast the cauliflower for about 20-25 minutes, or until fork-tender and beautifully caramelized. They should have a dark golden hue and a slightly crispy edge.

While the cauliflower is roasting, make the tahini-lemon sauce. In a small mixing bowl, combine tahini, lemon juice, minced garlic, and a pinch of salt. Stir to combine until smooth. If the sauce is too thick, add a little water (1-2 tablespoons) to reach your desired consistency, which should be pourable but thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
After removing the cauliflower from the oven, let it rest for 5 minutes. This helps to enhance its flavor and gives it a chance to soften slightly without losing texture.

To serve, drizzle the tahini-lemon sauce generously over the cauliflower steaks. Top with fresh pomegranate seeds, chopped parsley, and toasted almonds. You can toast the almonds by placing them in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently until fragrant and lightly browned. This adds a wonderful crunch and depth of flavor to the dish.
Enjoy your Whole-Roasted Cauliflower Steaks warm, either as a hearty main dish or a colorful side dish during your gatherings!

source_prompt: Eggplant parmigiana with crisp-edged eggplant, smoked mozzarella, basil-laced tomato sauce, baked until bubbling.
name: Crispy Eggplant Parmigiana with Smoked Mozzarella and Basil Tomato Sauce
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut the eggplant into 1 cm thick slices. Arrange the slices on a baking sheet and sprinkle lightly with salt. Let them sit for 30 minutes to draw out excess moisture.
Rinse the eggplant slices under cold water, pat dry with paper towels. They should feel slightly tender and less dense.

In a shallow dish, combine the egg with 60 ml of water, whisking until combined. In another dish, mix the breadcrumbs with a pinch of garlic powder, 1 g paprika, and some salt. Set up your dredging stations: the egg wash, followed by the breadcrumb mixture.
Dip each eggplant slice into the egg wash, then coat thoroughly in the breadcrumb mixture, pressing gently to adhere. Place back onto the baking sheet. Repeat until all slices are coated.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, adding 30 ml of whipped butter. Once hot, fry the eggplant slices for about 3-4 minutes per side, or until they turn golden brown and crispy. Work in batches if necessary, adding more butter as needed.

In a saucepan over medium heat, add the crushed tomatoes. Mince the garlic and add it to the tomatoes along with 2 g of dried basil and 2 g of salt. Allow it to simmer for about 5-8 minutes, stirring occasionally until it thickens slightly and the flavors meld.

In a large baking dish, layer half of the fried eggplant slices. Spoon over half of the tomato sauce, sprinkle with half of the smoked mozzarella, and half of the grated parmesan. Repeat layering with the remaining eggplant, tomato sauce, and cheeses.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheese is bubbling and golden brown on top. You should see some bubbling on the edges of the pan, and the aroma will fill the kitchen.
Once done, remove from oven and let it cool for 5-10 minutes to set. Serve garnished with fresh basil leaves, and enjoy the crispy, cheesy delight!

source_prompt: Spinach-and-ricotta gnocchi with brown butter, crispy sage, and lots of parmesan. Pillow-soft, properly seasoned.
name: Pillow-Soft Spinach and Ricotta Gnocchi with Brown Butter and Crispy Sage

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, add the fresh spinach and blanch for 1-2 minutes until wilted. Remove the spinach, shock in ice water to halt cooking, then drain and squeeze out excess moisture.
In a mixing bowl, combine the blanched spinach, ricotta, 50g of grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper. Stir until well combined, creating a green filling with a creamy texture.
Prepare the gnocchi dough by adding flour gradually to the spinach and ricotta mixture. Mix until it forms a soft dough that holds together without being sticky, about 5-7 minutes.
Divide the dough into four pieces. Roll each piece into a long rope about 1.5 cm thick, then cut into small 2 cm pieces to form gnocchi.
Using the back of a fork, gently press down on each piece to create ridges. Place the gnocchi on a lightly floured baking sheet and set aside.
Bring another pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Drop the gnocchi in batches, cooking until they float to the top, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
In a large skillet, melt the salted butter over medium heat. Allow it to brown slightly, watching for it to develop a nutty aroma and a deep golden color, about 4-5 minutes.
Add the cooked gnocchi to the skillet, tossing gently to coat in the brown butter. Cook for an additional 2 minutes until they are getting crispy and golden on the edges.
Add the sage leaves to the skillet, frying them in the butter until crispy, about 1-2 minutes. Be cautious not to burn the butter.

Finish the dish by adding the remaining Parmesan and a sprinkle of salt and pepper. Toss everything together to combine, then serve immediately, garnished with extra crispy sage and a drizzle of olive oil.

source_prompt: Red lentil and butternut squash dahl with coconut milk, ginger, mustard seeds, and a fresh coriander finish. Vegan.
name: Vibrant Butternut Squash and Lentil Dahl with Coconut Cream

ingredients.name: Babyfood, vegetable, butternut squash and corn

instructions: Rinse the lentils under cold water until the water runs clear. Set aside to drain.
Peel and dice the butternut squash into 2 cm cubes.
In a large pot, heat 30g of vegetable oil over medium heat. Add the diced onion and sauté for 4-5 minutes until translucent and fragrant.
Add 20g of minced garlic and 30g of minced ginger to the pot. Sauté for another 2 minutes until the mixture is aromatic and the garlic is lightly golden.
Sprinkle in 10g of cumin seeds, 5g of ground turmeric, 10g of coriander seed, and 5g of paprika. Toast the spices for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, stirring frequently to prevent burning.
Add the butternut squash cubes to the pot, stirring to coat them in the spiced onion mixture. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing the squash to begin softening.
Pour in 400g of coconut milk and add 150g of rinsed lentils along with 500ml of water. Stir well and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Season with 5g of salt and 2g of cracked black pepper. Cover the pot and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are tender and the squash is soft, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Once cooked, use a potato masher to slightly mash the dahl for a creamier consistency while leaving some chunks for texture. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Remove from heat and fold in 15g of lime juice and 5g of chopped fresh cilantro for brightness.
Let the dahl rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with more cilantro if desired, and enjoy hot with rice or naan.

source_prompt: Roasted butternut squash and sage pasta with brown butter, toasted hazelnuts, a grating of parmesan, and chili flakes.
name: Roasted Butternut Squash and Sage Pasta with Brown Butter and Hazelnuts

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F) for roasting the butternut squash.
Peel and cube 400g of butternut squash into uniform pieces, about 2cm wide. Toss the cubes in a bowl with 30g of olive oil, 2g of salt, and 2g of black pepper until well coated.

Spread the squash on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and roast in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes, stirring halfway through, until tender and caramelized, with a golden color and sweet aroma.

While the squash is roasting, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add 240g of dry pasta and cook according to package instructions until al dente, usually around 8-10 minutes. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water before draining the pasta.

In a skillet, melt 100g of salted butter over medium heat. Continue cooking it for about 5-7 minutes until it starts to foam and turn golden brown, stirring occasionally. Watch carefully for a nutty aroma and amber color.
Add 5g of ground sage to the brown butter and stir for 30 seconds to bloom the flavor. Then, add the roasted butternut squash to the skillet.
Add the drained pasta to the skillet along with a splash of reserved pasta water (about 100ml) to create a sauce. Stir until everything is well combined.
Chop 50g of hazelnuts roughly and add them to the pasta, squeezing in some fresh juice if desired (not included as an ingredient). Adjust seasoning with extra salt and black pepper to taste.
Just before serving, grate 30g of parmesan cheese over the top of the pasta, followed by a sprinkle of 5g of chili powder for heat. Mix until creamy and serve hot.

source_prompt: Sweet potato and black bean tacos with chipotle crema, pickled red onion, and fresh coriander. Charred corn tortillas.
name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos with Chipotle Crema and Pickled Red Onion

ingredients.name: Sweet potato, cooked, boiled, without skin

instructions: Preheat a skillet over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of oil, then add the diced onions. Sauté for about 3-4 minutes until they become translucent and fragrant.

Add the cooked sweet potato to the skillet and mash gently with a fork. Incorporate the cumin, salt, and pepper. Cook for an additional 4-5 minutes, letting the flavors meld and the sweet potato become slightly crispy on the edges.
Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the sour cream with the chipotle in adobo sauce, adjusting the amount of chipotle to taste. Mix well and set aside to allow the flavors to develop.
In a jar, combine the sliced red onions with the cider vinegar and a pinch of salt. Let them sit for at least 10 minutes to pickle and soften, stirring occasionally.
In a separate pan, char the corn tortillas over medium heat, about 30 seconds per side until they are warm and have some brown spots. Keep them warm by wrapping in a cloth or foil.
To assemble the tacos, start by placing a generous spoonful of the sweet potato mixture on each tortilla.
Top with black beans, a drizzle of chipotle crema, and a spoonful of pickled onions.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and a squirt of fresh lime juice for brightness. Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side for added acidity.
Enjoy your tacos with your favorite sides, such as rice or a fresh salad.

source_prompt: Greek spanakopita — spinach, feta, dill, and spring onion baked between crackling layers of filo with melted butter.
name: Golden Spanakopita with Spinach and Feta
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F) to get it ready for baking the spanakopita.
In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil over medium heat. Add 100g of chopped onions and sauté for about 4-5 minutes until they are soft and translucent, releasing their sweet aroma.

Add 300g of fresh spinach to the pan, stirring it in with the onions. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until the spinach wilts down and its vibrant green color brightens up. Drain excess water if the spinach releases too much liquid.

Remove the pan from the heat and let the mixture cool slightly. Then, crumble in 200g of feta cheese, followed by 10g of chopped dill, and 30g of fresh lemon juice. Season with 5g of salt and 1g of black pepper. Mix everything well until combined.
On a clean surface, lay out 6-8 sheets of filo pastry, brushing each layer with melted 30g of butter before adding the next sheet. This creates a crispy and flaky texture that you will love!

Once layered, spoon the spinach and feta filling along one edge of the filo, shaping it into a log or rectangle shape. Carefully fold in the edges and roll the pastry tightly around the filling to create a parcel or log shape.
Place the filled spanakopita onto a baking tray lined with parchment paper, seam side down. Brush the top with remaining melted butter for a golden crust during baking.
Bake in the preheated oven for 25-30 minutes or until the pastry is golden brown and crisp. The aroma of baked pastry should fill your kitchen, promising a delicious bite!
Once baked, remove from the oven and allow it to cool for a few minutes before slicing. Serve warm, garnished with extra dill and lemon wedges if desired.
Enjoy your spanakopita with a crisp salad or yogurt dip to balance the rich flavors!

source_prompt: 20-minute Korean ground beef bowls over rice with a soy-sesame glaze, quick-pickled cucumber, scallion, and toasted sesame.
name: Korean Ground Beef Bowls with Soy-Sesame Glaze and Quick-Pickled Cucumbers
instructions: Start by preparing the rice. Rinse 250g of rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Combine the rinsed rice with 500ml of water, a pinch of salt in a medium pot, and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce the heat to low, cover it, and let it simmer for about 15-20 minutes until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.

Meanwhile, slice 100g of cucumber into thin rounds for pickling. In a small bowl, combine the sliced cucumber with 30g of cider vinegar, 15g of brown sugar, and a pinch of salt. Mix well and let it sit for 10-15 minutes to pickle while you continue with the rest of the dish, stirring occasionally to ensure even pickling.

In a large skillet, heat 20g of canola oil over medium-high heat. Once hot, add 10g minced garlic and 10g minced ginger. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden, being careful not to burn them.

Add 500g of ground beef to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spatula. Let it sear for about 4-5 minutes without stirring to develop a nice brown crust. Season with 5g of salt and 1g of black pepper as it cooks.

Once browned, stir the beef to break it apart evenly. Add 60g of soy sauce to the pan, mixing well to combine. Allow it to simmer for about 3-4 minutes, letting the flavors meld while stirring occasionally.

While the beef simmers, chop 50g of scallions, separating the green and white parts. Add the white parts to the beef during the last minute of cooking for a slight bite, and reserve the green parts for garnishing.

Prepare to serve by fluffing the rice with a fork after it has finished cooking. Divide the rice into bowls, topping each serving with the beef mixture and a generous portion of the quick-pickled cucumbers.
Garnish each bowl with toasted sesame seeds and the reserved green parts of the scallions for a pop of color and flavor.

source_prompt: One-pan lemon-oregano chicken thighs with potatoes and red onion — everything roasts on one sheet, 35 minutes total.
name: Lemon-Oregano Roasted Chicken Thighs with Potatoes and Red Onion

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F). This high temperature will ensure a crispy finish on the chicken and potatoes.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the chicken thighs (about 800g) with the olive oil (60g), lemon juice from the lemons (about 120g), dried oregano (10g), paprika (5g), salt (7g), black pepper (5g), fresh thyme (10g), and fresh rosemary (10g). Stir until the chicken is well coated in the marinade. Allow it to marinate for at least 10 minutes for the flavors to infuse.
While the chicken is marinating, wash and chop the potatoes (600g) into even-sized chunks (about 3-4 cm). A uniform size will ensure they cook evenly.
Peel the sweet onions (100g) and slice them into thick wedges. This will add sweetness and depth when roasting.

On a large baking sheet, spread out the chopped potatoes (600g) and onion wedges (300g) in a single layer. Drizzle with a bit more olive oil if desired, and season with salt (to taste) and black pepper. Toss them to ensure they are mixed evenly.
Transfer the marinated chicken thighs onto the baking sheet, nestling them among the potatoes and onions. This will allow the chicken juices to flavor the vegetables as they roast.

Place the baking sheet in the preheated oven and roast for 25-30 minutes. You want the chicken skin to be golden brown and the internal temperature to reach 75°C (165°F). You'll see the potatoes edges getting crisp and the onions caramelizing. The aroma will be irresistible!
After about 25 minutes, check on the chicken and vegetables. If desired, you can turn the potatoes and onions for even browning.
When everything is cooked, remove the baking sheet from the oven and allow the chicken to rest for about 5 minutes. This helps to keep the chicken juicy.
Serve the roasted chicken thighs hot, garnished with fresh lemon wedges and sprinkled with additional fresh herbs if desired. Enjoy your flavorful one-pan meal!

source_prompt: 15-minute creamy garlic shrimp pasta with parsley, chili flakes, lemon zest, and parmesan. Genuinely fast, properly seasoned.
name: 15-Minute Creamy Garlic Shrimp Pasta
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil over high heat.

Add 200g of enriched pasta to the boiling water. Cook for 8-10 minutes or until al dente. Look for a tender but firm texture in the pasta. Drain and set aside, reserving a bit of the pasta water for later.
While the pasta is cooking, finely chop 10g of raw garlic and set aside. You will smell its pungency as you chop.
In a large skillet, heat 15g of olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the chopped garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Add 200g of cooked shrimp to the skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes until the shrimp are warmed through and start to develop a light golden hue. The aroma of garlic and shrimp should fill the air.

Sprinkle in 3g of chili powder, along with 5g of salt and 3g of ground black pepper. Stir to combine, allowing the spices to bloom for about 1 minute. You'll notice the shrimp taking on a more vibrant color.

Pour in 120g of heavy cream, stirring to blend it with the shrimp and garlic. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. You should see small bubbles forming around the edges of the skillet after about 1-2 minutes.

Add the cooked pasta to the creamy shrimp sauce, tossing to coat evenly. If the sauce is too thick, add a splash of reserved pasta water until it reaches a silky consistency. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed with more salt or pepper.
Finely chop 10g of fresh parsley and zest a small piece of lemon (about 10g). Stir both into the pasta, enhancing freshness and brightness. The dish should now smell vibrant and flavorful.
Serve immediately, garnishing each portion with 30g of grated parmesan cheese. Enjoy the creamy, garlicky delight with a hint of spice!

source_prompt: 25-minute miso-glazed salmon over steamed rice with sesame broccoli. Glaze caramelises under the broiler.
name: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Sesame Broccoli and Steamed Rice

ingredients.name: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
Onions, cooked, boiled, drained, with salt
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu), low sodium

instructions: Preheat your broiler to high.
In a small bowl, combine 30g of miso, 15g of rice bran oil, 15g of soy sauce, 10g of grated ginger, and the juice from half a lime. Stir until smooth.
Place 400g of salmon on a lined baking sheet. Season the salmon with salt and pepper (to taste) and brush half of the miso glaze evenly across the tops.
Broil the salmon for 6-8 minutes, keeping a close eye until the top is caramelized and the fish is opaque in the center; the glaze should be bubbly and slightly charred.
While the salmon is broiling, rinse 150g of rice and cook it according to package instructions. Fluff and set aside when done.
In a medium pot, bring water to a boil. Steam 250g of broccoli over the pot, covered, for about 5-7 minutes or until vibrant green and tender but still crisp.
Remove the broccoli from heat and toss it with 5g of sesame seeds, 10g of sesame butter paste, and a squeeze of lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary.
After the salmon is finished broiling, brush the remaining glaze on top of the salmon and return to the broiler for 1-2 more minutes for a final caramelization.
To serve, spoon 150g of rice onto each plate, top with the glazed salmon, and arrange broccoli alongside. Garnish with sliced scallions and a sprinkle of sesame seeds.

source_prompt: 25-minute chickpea curry with spinach, coconut milk, and warm spices. Pantry-friendly, vegan, served with basmati rice.
name: Spiced Chickpea and Spinach Curry with Coconut Cream
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium heat and add 30g of vegetable oil. Allow it to heat up for about 1 minute until shimmering.
Add 100g of diced onions to the skillet, sauté for 4-5 minutes until softened and translucent, stirring occasionally. The aroma should be fragrant and slightly sweet.
Stir in 15g of minced garlic and 15g of minced ginger. Sauté for an additional 2-3 minutes until fragrant, and the garlic turns a light golden color.
Sprinkle in 15g of curry powder, 5g of cumin seed, and 5g of coriander seed, and sauté for 1-2 minutes. Toasting the spices enhances their flavor and aroma.
Add 400g of canned chickpeas (drained and rinsed) to the skillet, stirring well to combine everything. Cook for about 3-4 minutes until they start to warm up.
Pour in 400g of coconut milk, stirring to create a creamy sauce. Season with 5g of salt and 2g of black pepper, adjusting to taste.
Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer by increasing the heat slightly. Allow it to simmer for 5-7 minutes, checking occasionally until thickened slightly.
Fold in 200g of fresh spinach, letting it wilt for about 2-3 minutes. It should be vibrant green and tender but still hold its shape.
Squeeze in 10g of fresh lime juice for brightness and acidity, stirring to combine well. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.
Meanwhile, cook 200g of brown rice according to package instructions in a rice cooker or pot, usually 30-40 minutes.
Serve the chickpea curry hot over a bed of brown rice, garnished with extra lime wedges if desired. Enjoy the rich, spiced aroma and flavors!

source_prompt: 20-minute caprese pasta salad with cherry tomato, fresh mozzarella, torn basil, balsamic glaze, and good olive oil. Eat warm or cold.
name: Vibrant Caprese Pasta Salad

ingredients.name: Mayonnaise, reduced fat, with olive oil

instructions: 1. Gather all ingredients and bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil over high heat.
2. Add 200g of fresh pasta to the boiling water. Cook according to package instructions until al dente, usually about 2-4 minutes. Taste occasionally; you want it firm but tender.
3. While the pasta cooks, chop 150g of mozzarella cheese into bite-sized cubes. Set aside in a large mixing bowl.
4. Drain the pasta and reserve a little pasta water. Add the hot pasta directly to the bowl with the mozzarella; the heat will melt the cheese slightly, adding creaminess.
5. Dice 150g of fresh orange tomatoes (or use any available fresh tomatoes) and add them to the pasta and mozzarella combination. Their juiciness will create a nice balance.
6. Tear 20g of fresh basil leaves and sprinkle them over the salad. The aroma of the basil will add a vibrant touch.

7. Drizzle 25g of balsamic vinegar and a light spoonful (10g) of mayonnaise with olive oil into the mixture. Toss everything gently but thoroughly to combine all flavors without breaking the cheese pieces.
8. If the salad appears dry, add a splash of the reserved pasta water to achieve your desired consistency.
9. Season with salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste, mixing well again to distribute the seasoning evenly.
10. Serve immediately for a warm dish or store in the fridge for a few minutes to enjoy it cold. The flavors will develop nicely as it rests. Enjoy the vibrant colors and aromas!

source_prompt: 25-minute steak fajitas with charred bell pepper and onion, warm flour tortillas, lime, and a quick guacamole.
name: Sizzling Steak Fajitas with Charred Veggies and Quick Guacamole
instructions: 1. **Prep the Ingredients**: Slice the top sirloin steak into thin strips (~1 cm) and season with salt, black pepper, and cumin. Let marinate for 10 minutes at room temperature while prepping vegetables.

2. **Sauté the Aromatics**: Heat 1 tablespoon of avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Once the oil shimmers (about 1 minute), add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant, avoiding browning.

3. **Cook the Steak**: Increase heat to high and add the seasoned steak to the skillet, spreading it into a single layer. Sear for 3-4 minutes without stirring to develop a brown crust, then stir and continue to cook for another 1-2 minutes until just cooked through. Remove from the skillet and set aside.

4. **Char the Vegetables**: In the same skillet, add another tablespoon of avocado oil. Once hot, add the sliced onions and bell peppers. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until they start to char and soften, stirring occasionally. They should be tender and slightly caramelized.

5. **Combine and Adjust Seasoning**: Return the steak to the skillet with the charred veggies. Toss everything together, adding salt and pepper to taste. Allow to cook together for an additional 2 minutes to meld flavors.

6. **Prepare the Tortillas**: While the veggies and steak are mingling, wrap flour tortillas in aluminum foil and place them in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for about 5-7 minutes until warmed through.
7. **Make Quick Guacamole**: In a bowl, mash the avocado with a fork. Squeeze in juice from half the lime and season with salt and chopped cilantro. Mix until combined but still chunky.

8. **Serve**: Remove everything from heat. Build your fajitas by spooning the steak and veggie mix onto a warm tortilla. Top with fresh jalapeno slices, guacamole, and a squeeze of lime juice for brightness and acidity.
9. **Enjoy**: Roll up the fajitas and serve with additional lime wedges on the side for a zesty finish.

source_prompt: 20-minute halloumi and quinoa bowls with herbed yogurt, cucumber, cherry tomato, mint, and a lemon-olive-oil dressing.
name: Fresh Quinoa Halloumi Bowls with Herbed Yogurt and Citrus Vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Sauce, pesto, CLASSICO, basil pesto, ready-to-serve
Sauce, pesto, BUITONI, pesto with basil, ready-to-serve, refrigerated

instructions: Rinse 150g of uncooked quinoa under cold water to remove any bitterness.

In a pot, add the rinsed quinoa with 300g of water. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Once boiling, reduce to low heat, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until the quinoa is fluffy and the water is absorbed. Remove from heat and let it rest for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.

While the quinoa cooks, prepare the herbed yogurt. In a bowl, combine 100g of nonfat mozzarella cheese, 50g of crumbled feta cheese, and 100g of cherry tomatoes (halved). Add 10g of fresh spearmint, finely chopped, and stir well to combine.

For the dressing, whisk together the juice of 50g lemon (about 2-3 tablespoons of juice) with 50g of extra virgin olive oil, a pinch of salt, and black pepper to taste. Add in 30g of basil pesto for flavor depth and mix well until emulsified.
Dice 150g of cucumber and add to the bowl with the cheeses and tomatoes. Drizzle in some of the lemon-olive oil dressing and toss gently to coat everything evenly.

Once the quinoa has rested, remove the lid and fluff with a fork. Gradually add the herbed cheese and tomato mix into the quinoa and gently fold it in to combine, ensuring not to mash the ingredients.
Divide the quinoa mixture into serving bowls and drizzle with additional lemon-olive oil dressing if desired. Garnish with additional fresh mint leaves on top for an aromatic finish.
Serve warm or at room temperature, enjoying a blend of textures and crisp refreshing flavors.

source_prompt: Slow-braised beef bourguignon with bacon lardons, pearl onions, mushrooms, and red wine. Cook Sunday, eats brilliantly over the next 4 days.
name: Classic Beef Bourguignon with Bacon Lardons and Pearl Onions
instructions: Prepare your ingredients: Dice 750g beef into 3cm cubes, slice 200g of bacon into lardons, and finely chop 20g garlic.

Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the bacon and cook for about 5-7 minutes until crispy and golden brown. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the bacon to a paper towel-lined plate, leaving the rendered fat in the pot.
In the fat left in the pot, add the beef cubes in batches, searing for 4-5 minutes per batch until browned on all sides. Remove and set aside with the bacon.

Add the sliced carrots and mushrooms to the pot, sautéing for about 5 minutes until they begin to soften. Then add the garlic and cook for an additional 1 minute until fragrant, stirring continuously.
Sprinkle in 10g dried thyme, add 3 dried bay leaves, and season with salt and black pepper (5g each). Stir well to coat the vegetables.
Return the beef and bacon back to the pot. Pour in 750g red wine and bring to a gentle simmer. Scrape the bottom of the pot with a wooden spoon to deglaze any brown bits stuck to the bottom.
Cover and reduce the heat to low, maintaining a low simmer. Cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the beef is tender and the flavors meld.
After cooking, remove the lid and let it simmer for an additional 30 minutes uncovered to thicken the sauce slightly. Taste for seasoning, adding more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh thyme leaves and accompanied by crusty bread or mashed potatoes for soaking up the flavorful sauce.

source_prompt: Big-batch chickpea, sweet potato, and coconut curry with spinach. Scales to 8 portions, freezes well, vegan.
name: Spiced Chickpea and Sweet Potato Coconut Curry with Spinach
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat until shimmering (about 2-3 minutes).
Add diced onions and sauté, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until translucent and fragrant.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger. Sauté for an additional 2 minutes, allowing the mix to become aromatic.
Add curry powder and cumin seeds, stirring continuously for 1-2 minutes to bloom the spices; they should become fragrant and deepen in color.
Chop the sweet potatoes into 2cm cubes and add to the pot. Stir well to coat in the spices and onion mixture, cooking for another 4-5 minutes until they start to soften.
Pour in vegetable broth and coconut milk. Bring to a gentle simmer while stirring, ensuring everything is combined (about 5 minutes).
Add the drained canned chickpeas, stirring carefully to avoid mashing them. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until sweet potatoes are tender but not falling apart.
Stir in fresh spinach, cooking for about 2-3 minutes until wilted. If using a lid, leave it off to maintain the curry's vibrant color.
Juice the limes into the curry, stirring to combine. Add salt to taste and adjust spices if necessary for desired heat and flavor. Let the curry simmer for an extra 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves before serving. Serve hot with rice or naan, ensuring a balance of flavors. Enjoy!

source_prompt: Slow-cooker shredded chicken tinga with chipotle, tomato, and oregano. A week of taco fillings, salad toppings, and rice-bowl protein.
name: Smoky Shredded Chicken Tinga with Chipotle and Oregano
instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 15g of chicken fat and allow it to melt until shimmering, releasing a rich aroma.

While the fat is heating, finely chop 100g of raw onions and 15g of garlic. Once the fat is ready, add the onions and sauté for about 5 minutes until they are translucent and lightly browned, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add the chopped garlic to the skillet and sauté for an additional 1-2 minutes, until fragrant. Be careful not to let the garlic burn, as it can become bitter.

Next, add 600g of raw ground chicken to the skillet. Use a spatula or wooden spoon to break it apart, stirring to incorporate with the aromatics. Cook for about 6-8 minutes until the chicken is browned and cooked through, stirring regularly to develop fond on the bottom of the pan.
Sprinkle in 5g of cumin seed, 5g of coriander seed, and 10g of dried oregano. Toast the spices for 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously to bloom their flavors and release their aromas.

Pour in the 400g of crushed canned tomatoes and 300g of canned onion soup into the skillet, mixing everything together well. Bring the mixture to a simmer, allowing it to cook for about 10 minutes. This helps to meld the flavors together.

While the mixture is simmering, dissolve 20g of chicken broth cubes in 500ml of hot water. After 10 minutes, add this broth to the skillet, along with 5g of black pepper and 5g of salt. Stir to combine and bring the mixture back to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low, cover the skillet, and let it simmer for an additional 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. This helps to further integrate the flavors and create a cohesive dish.
Once the mixture is finished cooking, taste and adjust the seasoning if needed. Squeeze in 20g of fresh lime juice for a bright finish, stirring it in gently.
Using two forks or meat claws, shred the chicken in the skillet, mixing it with the sauce. Allow it to rest for a few minutes to absorb the flavors before serving.
Serve the shredded chicken tinga warm as a taco filling, salad topping, or alongside rice.

source_prompt: Vegetarian lentil bolognese with a soffritto base, plenty of mushrooms for umami, and red wine. Sauces a week of pasta or polenta.
name: Umami-Packed Vegetarian Lentil Bolognese
instructions: Rinse the lentils under cold water and set aside.
Finely dice the onion, carrot, and celery to make a soffritto. Mince the garlic.

In a large pot over medium heat, add 50g of olive oil. Once hot, add the diced onions, carrot, and celery. Saute for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring frequently. The aroma should be sweet and fragrant.
Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute, until fragrant. Be cautious not to let it burn.
Stir in the mushrooms and cook for about 5 minutes until they release their moisture and begin to brown, stirring occasionally.
Add 200g of rinsed lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them in the vegetable mixture. Toast the lentils for about 2 minutes, enhancing their nuttiness.
Pour in 400g of crushed tomatoes and 300ml of water or vegetable broth. Mix well and bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.

Add the bay leaf and thyme, and season with 5g of salt and 1g of black pepper. Allow the sauce to simmer uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender and the sauce has thickened. Adjust the seasoning to taste, adding more salt or pepper if necessary.
Finish the sauce by stirring in 30g of red wine and simmer for another 5 minutes to meld the flavors together. The sauce should attain a rich color and a deep, savory aroma.
Remove the bay leaf before serving. Serve the lentil bolognese over pasta or polenta, garnished with fresh herbs if desired. Enjoy!

source_prompt: Moroccan chicken tagine with dried apricot, preserved lemon, toasted almond, and warm spices. Served over fluffy couscous.
name: Spiced Moroccan Chicken Tagine with Apricots and Toasted Almonds

ingredients.name: Soup, chicken broth cubes, dry, prepared with water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large tagine or heavy-bottom pot over medium heat.
Add finely chopped onion and sauté for about 5-7 minutes until translucent and fragrant.
Stir in minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for another minute until aromatic.
Add ground chicken to the pot, breaking it apart with a spatula. Cook for about 6-8 minutes until browned, stirring occasionally.
Sprinkle in paprika, cumin, coriander, and cinnamon, stirring well to coat the chicken and blooming the spices for 2-3 minutes until they are fragrant.
Incorporate the dried apricots and pour in the chicken broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer and reduce the heat to low, covering the pot.
Let simmer for 20 minutes to allow the flavors to develop and the apricots to soften, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the lemon juice and season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep simmering for an additional 5 minutes.
While the tagine finishes, cook the couscous according to package instructions, usually combining it with boiling water and letting it sit covered for about 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and serve it as a bed on individual plates.
Top the fluffy couscous with the spiced chicken tagine, garnishing with toasted almonds for crunch. Enjoy!

source_prompt: Texas-style three-bean chili with chuck steak, ancho, and chipotle. Better on day two. Cornbread for sopping.
name: Texas-Style Three-Bean Chili with Chuck Steak
instructions: Prepare the ingredients: Dice the beef into 2 cm cubes, finely chop the onion, mince the garlic, and chop the celery into small pieces. Set aside.
In a large pot, heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Season the beef cubes with salt and black pepper.
Sear the beef in batches, making sure not to overcrowd the pot. Cook for about 4-5 minutes per side until they are nicely browned and develop a crust. Remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add the diced onions and celery. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until the onions are translucent and fragrant. The fond left in the pot will add depth to the chili.
Stir in the minced garlic, ancho chili, chipotle chili, cumin, oregano, and cayenne pepper. Cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, stirring frequently, until the spices bloom and release their aroma.
Add the beef back into the pot along with canned tomatoes, kidney beans, pinto beans, and black beans. Stir well to combine.
Pour in 500 ml of beef stock to maintain a good texture and flavor. Bring to a vigorous simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and let simmer for at least 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.
Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or additional spices as desired. After simmering, the chili should be thickened and the flavors meld.
While the chili is simmering, preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prepare cornbread using cornmeal (or mix as per package instructions) to complement the chili's flavors.
Serve the chili hot in bowls, garnished with a dollop of sour cream and fresh cilantro if available. Accompany with warm cornbread for sopping up the delicious sauce.

source_prompt: Sunday roast chicken with crispy potatoes, glazed carrots, and a pan-gravy. Leftover chicken becomes sandwiches and soup the rest of the week.
name: Sunday Roast Chicken with Crispy Potatoes and Glazed Carrots
instructions: Preheat your oven to 220°C (425°F) to create a crisp exterior for the chicken and potatoes.

Rinse the whole chicken under cold water, pat it dry with paper towels. Season generously inside and out with salt and black pepper, about 10g and 5g respectively. Place thyme and rosemary sprigs inside the cavity for added flavor.

Heat 30g of salted butter in a large oven-proof skillet over medium-high heat. Once melted and bubbling, place the chicken breast-side down and sear for 5-6 minutes until it turns golden brown. You should hear a satisfying sizzle, and the skin will start to crisp.

Flip the chicken onto its back and transfer the skillet directly into the preheated oven. Roast for 1 hour or until the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F) and the skin is golden brown and crispy. Baste with the melted butter in the pan halfway through.

While the chicken roasts, scrub and cut the potatoes into even-sized chunks, about 5cm. Toss the potatoes in a bowl with 30g of olive oil, salt (5g), pepper (3g), and rosemary. Make sure the potatoes are fully coated with oil and seasoning.
