Transfer the seasoned potatoes onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and roast them in the oven alongside the chicken for 45 minutes or until they are crispy and golden, turning them halfway through for even cooking.

For the glazed carrots, peel the carrots and cut them into sticks. In a medium saucepan, melt the remaining 70g of butter over medium heat. Add the carrots and sauté for 5-6 minutes until they start to soften. Add 100ml of chicken broth, cover, and simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes until tender.
Once the chicken is done, remove it from the oven and let it rest for 15 minutes before carving. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring moist meat.

To make the gravy, place the skillet with the chicken drippings over medium heat. Add 200ml of chicken broth and scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan (this adds great flavor). Simmer for 5 minutes, then drizzle in the lemon juice and season to taste with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the carved chicken with the crispy potatoes and glazed carrots on the side. Drizzle the gravy over the chicken and enjoy your Sunday feast!
For leftovers, store any uncooked chicken in the refrigerator for sandwiches or soup throughout the week.

source_prompt: Provençal ratatouille — slow-roasted summer vegetables (eggplant, zucchini, bell pepper, tomato) layered with garlic and herbes de Provence. Vegan-friendly.
name: Provençal Ratatouille: Slow-Roasted Summer Vegetables

ingredients.name: Sauce, pesto, BUITONI, pesto with basil, ready-to-serve, refrigerated

instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Gather fresh vegetables and make sure they are washed and dried to prepare for roasting.
Cut the eggplant into 1.5 cm cubes, ensuring they are roughly the same size.
Slice the zucchini into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Cut the sweet red peppers into strips.

In a large mixing bowl, combine the eggplant, zucchini, red pepper, and chopped tomatoes. Add a pinch of salt and black pepper to taste along with the garlic powder and paprika, mixing until evenly coated.
Drizzle olive oil over the vegetables, about 30 grams, ensuring that they are well coated to enhance roasting.
Spread the vegetable mixture evenly on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper for easy removal later, making sure they are not overcrowded for even roasting.
Place the baking sheet in the preheated oven and roast for 35-40 minutes, stirring halfway through. The veggies should be tender and slightly caramelized, giving off a rich, earthy aroma.
Check for seasoning at the 30-minute mark. Adjust with more salt, black pepper, or additional spices as preferred, tossing to combine.
Once roasted, remove the vegetables from the oven and let them rest for about 5 minutes. This allows the flavors to meld.

Fold in the dried basil and oregano before serving to add fresh herbal notes that uplift the dish. Serve warm, drizzling with a bit of pesto to finish on each portion. Enjoy your Provençal Ratatouille!

source_prompt: Greek baked feta with cherry tomatoes, olives, oregano, and olive oil — tossed through orzo. The feta melts into a sauce.
name: Mediterranean Feta and Tomato Orzo Bake
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F). This temperature will allow the feta to melt beautifully and the tomatoes to roast without burning.

In a large baking dish, add 300g of halved red ripe tomatoes and 100g of halved green tomatoes. Drizzle with 25g of olive oil, allowing their sweet aroma to fill the kitchen, and sprinkle with 5g of salt. Toss well to coat the tomatoes in the oil and salt, then roast in the oven for 20-25 minutes until the tomatoes are blistered and juicy.

While the tomatoes roast, cook 200g of orzo in a large pot of salted boiling water for about 9 minutes or until al dente. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking. The orzo should have a firm yet tender texture when done. Drain and set aside.

In a medium skillet over medium heat, add the remaining 25g of olive oil. Once heated, add 20g of minced garlic and sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant and lightly golden, taking care not to burn it.

Once the tomatoes are roasted, remove the baking dish from the oven and create a well in the center. Crumble 200g of feta cheese into the well. The warm tomatoes will help melt the cheese, infusing it with flavor.
Reduce the oven temperature to 180°C (350°F) and return the baking dish to the oven. Bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the feta is soft and slightly golden on top.

After baking, remove the dish from the oven and gently fold in the cooked orzo, 100g of ripe olives, and 10g of dried oregano. Make sure to combine everything well, allowing the orzo to absorb the flavors of the tomatoes, olives, and feta.
Taste and adjust the seasoning with additional salt or freshly cracked black pepper according to your preference. Serve warm, garnished with fresh herbs if desired.

source_prompt: Danish smørrebrød with cold-smoked salmon, dill horseradish cream, pickled radish, and crispy rye. Open-faced and architectural.
name: Architectural Danish Smørrebrød with Cold-Smoked Salmon
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine 200g of medium rye flour and 5g of chopped chives. Gradually add 100ml of water while mixing to form a dough. Rest for 15 minutes.
Preheat your oven to 200°C (392°F). Roll out the dough to a thickness of about 0.5cm. Place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake the rye flatbreads in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes or until they are crispy and lightly golden. Let cool.

Meanwhile, prepare the cream by mixing 100g of light sour cream with 30g of prepared horseradish, 10g of finely chopped dill weed, 15g of lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed. Set aside.
Slice 50g of fresh radishes thinly and transfer them to a bowl. Add 10g of cider vinegar, a pinch of salt, and let them pickle for about 10 minutes.
Take the cooled rye flatbreads and spread a layer of the horseradish cream evenly across each piece, leaving a small border.
Artfully arrange 100-150g of cold-smoked salmon on top of the cream. Fluent, wavy layers will give that architectural appeal.
Scatter the pickled radishes over the salmon, followed by a sprinkle of 15g of capers and a few fennel seeds for an aromatic finish.
For garnish, roughly chop additional dill and chives, and sprinkle them over the top for a fresh green touch.
Drizzle a bit of lemon juice and a light pinch of salt before serving. Enjoy your Danish smørrebrød beautifully arranged and ready to impress!

source_prompt: Thai green chicken curry with bamboo shoots, Thai basil, kaffir lime leaves, and creamy coconut milk. Serve over jasmine rice.
name: Creamy Thai Green Chicken Curry

ingredients.name: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Soy sauce, reduced sodium, made from hydrolyzed vegetable protein

instructions: Chop the onion, garlic, and ginger finely. Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion to the skillet and sauté for 3-4 minutes until translucent and aromatic.
Stir in the minced garlic and ginger, cooking for an additional 1-2 minutes until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Push the onion mix to the side and add the chicken, searing it on medium-high heat for about 5-7 minutes until lightly browned.
Incorporate bamboo shoots and cook together for 2-3 minutes to combine the flavors and warm through.
Pour in the coconut milk, stirring to combine, then add soy sauce and brown sugar. Bring the mixture to a simmer.
Add any additional herbs and spices you have on hand to deepen the flavor and adjust seasoning to taste.
Allow the curry to gently simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot over freshly cooked jasmine rice. Garnish with any available herbs or fresh lime juice to brighten the dish.

source_prompt: Japanese chicken karaage — soy-and-ginger marinated thigh, dredged in potato starch, double-fried for shatter-crisp edges. With shiso slaw and Kewpie.
name: Crispy Chicken Karaage with Shiso Slaw

ingredients.name: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)

instructions: Prepare the chicken by cutting 500g of ground raw chicken into bite-sized pieces for the karaage.
In a medium bowl, combine 60g of soy sauce, 20g of finely grated ginger, and 15g of cider vinegar. Mix well.
Add the chicken pieces into the marinade and stir until evenly coated. Allow the chicken to marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator, enhancing the flavors.
While the chicken marinates, prepare the slaw. In a large mixing bowl, combine 100g of thinly sliced raw cabbage and 50g of grated raw carrots.
In a separate small bowl, mix 40g of mayonnaise with 15g of brown sugar and a splash of cider vinegar. Whisk to create a creamy dressing.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrots. Toss gently to combine and set aside in the refrigerator for flavors to meld.
After the marinade time, remove the chicken from the refrigerator. Heat 500g of vegetable oil in a deep frying pan over medium-high heat until it reaches 180°C (350°F).
Dredge the marinated chicken pieces in potato starch, ensuring they are well-coated to create a crispy texture.
Once the oil is hot, carefully add the dredged chicken pieces in batches, frying for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through, turning halfway for even cooking.
Remove the fried chicken and let it rest on a paper towel-lined plate to absorb excess oil, ensuring the coating remains crisp.
Serve the crispy chicken karaage on a plate alongside the shiso slaw and drizzle with additional mayonnaise if desired.

source_prompt: Vietnamese bún chả — caramelised grilled pork patties over rice noodles with mountain of herbs, pickled vegetables, and nuoc cham dipping sauce.
name: Caramelised Grilled Pork Bún Chả with Herbs and Pickles

ingredients.name: Soy sauce made from hydrolyzed vegetable protein

instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine the ground pork with the grated ginger, minced garlic, soy sauce, brown sugar, and a pinch of chili powder. Mix until well blended. Set aside to marinate for 30 minutes to an hour in the refrigerator.
While the pork is marinating, prepare the rice noodles. Cook the noodles according to the package instructions, generally boiling them for 4-6 minutes until tender. Drain and set aside.

In a small bowl, mix lime juice, cider vinegar, and a bit of soy sauce to create a dressing for your pickled vegetables. Thinly slice the carrots and cucumber, and toss these in the dressing. Let them marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Preheat a grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Shape the marinated pork mixture into small patties, about 100 grams each.
Grill the pork patties for about 4-5 minutes on each side or until they are nicely caramelized and cooked through. The exterior should have a golden brown color, and the inside should be juicy.
Once the pork is done, remove from heat and let it rest for a few minutes. This helps retain juices and heat.
To serve, divide the cooked rice noodles into bowls. Top the noodles with the grilled pork patties and a generous heap of the pickled vegetables.
Garnish with fresh cilantro and mint leaves. Offer lime wedges for additional freshness and acidity.

source_prompt: Sichuan kung pao chicken with dried red chili, Sichuan peppercorn for that numbing tingle, peanuts, scallion, and a glossy black-vinegar sauce.
name: Numbing Sichuan Kung Pao Chicken

ingredients.name: Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Salad dressing, peppercorn dressing, commercial, regular
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
Sauce, peanut, made from peanut butter, water, soy sauce

instructions: 1. **Prepare the ingredients:** Begin by finely chopping 500g of ground chicken and placing it in a bowl. Mince 10g of garlic and 10g of ginger. Chop 30g of scallions, keeping the white and green parts separate.
2. **Make the sauce:** In a separate bowl, mix 30g of soy sauce, 50g of peanut butter, and 15g of cider vinegar. Whisk together until smooth and set aside for later.
3. **Marinate the chicken:** Season the ground chicken with 5g of salt, 5g of sugar, and 5g of black pepper. Allow it to marinate for about 15 minutes to enhance the flavor before cooking.
4. **Heat the oil:** In a large skillet or wok, heat 30g of wheat germ oil over medium-high heat until it shimmers and is nearly smoking. This will provide a fragrant base for cooking.

5. **Brown the chicken:** Add the marinated ground chicken to the hot oil. Using a spatula, break up the chicken into small pieces. Cook for about 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is browned and no longer pink.
6. **Add aromatics:** Add the minced garlic, ginger, and the white parts of the scallions to the skillet. Stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant, ensuring the garlic doesn’t burn.

7. **Create the sauce base:** Pour the previously mixed sauce into the skillet. Add 20g of peppercorn dressing and stir everything together, allowing it to simmer for about 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and clings to the chicken.
8. **Incorporate peanuts:** Mix in 50g of raw Spanish peanuts, stirring to combine well. Cook for an additional 2 minutes for the peanuts to absorb some of the flavors.
9. **Adjust seasoning:** Taste the mixture and adjust seasoning if necessary, adding more salt or sugar as needed. The balance of flavor is critical in Kung Pao chicken.
10. **Finish with scallions:** Finally, fold in the green parts of the sliced scallions, allowing them to wilt slightly. This should take about 1 minute.
11. **Plate and garnish:** Serve the Kung Pao chicken hot over steamed rice or noodles, garnished with additional peanuts if desired.
12. **Enjoy:** Relish the complex flavors and textures of this classic dish, feeling the numbing effect of peppercorns alongside the savory and sweet elements.

source_prompt: Korean bibimbap with sesame-marinated beef bulgogi, an array of seasoned vegetables, a runny fried egg, and a generous spoon of gochujang.
name: Vibrant Bibimbap with Sesame Beef Bulgogi

ingredients.name: Squash, summer, zucchini, includes skin, raw
Soy sauce made from soy and wheat (shoyu)
Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb), raw
Soy sauce made from hydrolyzed vegetable protein

instructions: Prepare the Beef Bulgogi: Thinly slice 300g of beef bologna, marinate with 30g of soy sauce, 15g of sesame paste, and a dash of black pepper. Let it rest for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld.

In a pan, heat 1 tbsp of sesame oil over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated beef in a single layer. Sear for about 4-5 minutes until browned and slightly caramelized. Remove from heat and set aside, keeping warm.

Prepare the vegetables: Peel and julienne 150g carrots. Chop 100g of spinach. Slice 100g of mushrooms thinly and cut 150g zucchini into half-moons. Score a few lines into the surface of each cucumber, then slice into thin rounds.

In the same pan with leftover juices from the beef, add the sliced carrots and sauté for 3-4 minutes until tender but still bright in color. Add a pinch of salt and pepper to taste. Remove and keep warm.
Add the spinach to the pan and sauté until wilted, about 2-3 minutes. Season lightly with salt. Remove from the pan and keep warm.
In the same pan, add the sliced mushrooms and zucchini, cooking for about 3-4 minutes until they are soft and slightly browned. Season with a pinch of salt.

To cook the eggs, heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add a little oil if needed. Crack 2 eggs into the pan and fry until the edges are crisp and the yolks are runny, about 2-3 minutes. Season with a little salt and set aside.
To assemble, in a large bowl or platter, arrange the cooked rice as the base. On top, layer the sautéed vegetables, bulgogi beef, and place the fried eggs on top.
Garnish with chopped scallions and drizzle with additional sesame sauce if desired. Serve with a generous spoonful of gochujang on the side for spicy flavor.

source_prompt: Thai pad krapow gai — minced chicken stir-fried with garlic, bird's-eye chili, and Thai holy basil. Crown with a crisp-edged fried egg.
name: Spicy Thai Basil Chicken with Fried Egg

ingredients.name: Sauce, peppers, hot, chili, mature red, canned
Sauce, pesto, CLASSICO, basil pesto, ready-to-serve
Sauce, peppers, hot, chili, mature red, canned

instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add 30g of vegetable oil; allow it to shimmer, about 1-2 minutes.
Add 20g of minced garlic to the oil, sautéing until fragrant, approximately 30 seconds to 1 minute, maintaining a light golden color.

Introduce 400g of ground chicken to the skillet. Use a wooden spoon to break it up. Cook for about 5-7 minutes until browned and no longer pink, stirring occasionally to build fond at the bottom of the skillet.
Add in 30g of hot red chili peppers, finely chopped. Stir and cook for 1-2 minutes until they become tender, releasing their aroma.
In a smaller bowl, mix 20g of soy sauce and 10g of granulated sugar until combined. Pour this mixture into the skillet and stir to coat chicken evenly, allowing the flavors to meld for 2-3 minutes.
Add 30g of fresh basil leaves, folding them gently into the chicken until just wilted. Turn off the heat to prevent overcooking the basil, which should remain vibrant green.
In another pan, add a teaspoon of oil and heat over medium heat. Crack 2 eggs into the pan, frying them sunny-side up until the whites are set, roughly 3-4 minutes. Aim for crisp edges.
Plate the spicy basil chicken on a bed of rice or noodles. Top each serving with a fried egg, allowing the yolk to be runny for added richness when broken.
Squeeze fresh lime juice over the dish before serving, adding brightness to the flavors. Garnish with extra basil leaves if desired. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary before serving.

source_prompt: Indian palak paneer — cubes of fresh paneer in a smooth, spiced spinach gravy with ginger, garlic, and a swirl of cream.
name: Creamy Spiced Spinach and Paneer Delight
instructions: Prepare the spinach by rinsing it thoroughly under cold water, then roughly chop it. Gather the garlic, ginger, and other spices before starting.
In a large skillet, heat 20g of vegetable oil over medium heat until shimmering, about 1 minute. Add 100g of chopped onions and sauté for 4-5 minutes until they are translucent and slightly golden.
Add 20g of minced garlic and 10g of freshly grated ginger to the skillet. Sauté for an additional 1-2 minutes until aromatic—don't let them burn!
Stir in 5g of cumin seeds, 5g of chili powder, and 2g of turmeric. Stir to toast the spices for about 1 minute until they release their fragrance, stirring constantly.
Add the chopped spinach (200g) to the skillet. Cook for about 5-7 minutes until wilted and tender. Season with salt (3g) and fresh black pepper (1g) to taste.
Add 100g of cooked tomatoes into the spinach mixture, stir well to combine, and let simmer for another 3 minutes.
Using an immersion blender, blend the mixture until smooth. If you prefer a chunkier sauce, blend partially to retain some texture.
Cube 200g of fresh paneer and add it to the spinach gravy, gently folding it in without breaking the cubes. Let it simmer for another 5 minutes to allow the paneer to warm through and absorb flavor.
Slowly stir in 60g of cream and 40g of sour cream, stirring until well combined to create a rich and creamy texture.
Finish with chopped fresh cilantro (15g) mixed into the dish just before serving for a burst of freshness. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Serve it hot with naan or rice.

source_prompt: Creamy mushroom risotto with white wine, parmesan, a knob of butter for mantecatura, and a few drops of truffle oil. 4 servings.
name: Elegant Mushroom Risotto with White Wine and Parmesan

ingredients.name: Soup, chicken broth, low sodium, canned

instructions: Prepare the broth: In a saucepan, combine 500ml chicken broth with 500ml vegetable broth. Heat over low heat until warm, but not boiling (keeping it warm will help it integrate smoothly into the risotto).
Mushroom prep: Clean 300g of white mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them. Set aside about 50g for garnishing later.
Sauté the aromatics: In a large pot, melt 50g of salted butter over medium heat. Once melted, add 100g finely chopped onions and sauté for about 3-4 minutes until translucent and soft.
Add garlic: Incorporate 10g of minced garlic into the pot and sauté for an additional minute until fragrant, stirring frequently to avoid burning.
Cook the mushrooms: Add the sliced mushrooms (250g) to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until browned and reduced in size. The mushrooms should release their moisture and become aromatic.

Toast the rice: Add 200g of rice crackers (this represents the Arborio rice in a substitute method) to the mixture, stirring continuously for 2-3 minutes until slightly translucent around the edges. This will enhance the nuttiness of the rice.

Deglaze with wine: Pour in 150g of dry white wine, stirring constantly. Allow it to simmer until the liquid is almost fully absorbed, about 3 minutes, which will lift any flavorful bits from the bottom of the pot.

Incorporate the broth: Begin adding the warm broth (about a ladleful at a time) to the rice mixture, stirring frequently. Allow it to simmer and absorb before adding more broth. Repeat this process until you have used about 1 liter of the combined broths and the rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes.

Finish the risotto: Once the rice is cooked to your desired firmness, remove from heat. Stir in 100g of hard Parmesan cheese and a pinch of saffron (0.2g). Adjust the seasoning with 5g of salt and 2g of black pepper. The risotto should be creamy and rich.
Add creaminess: Before serving, fold in an additional 50g of cream cheese to enrich the risotto, making it incredibly creamy and luxurious.
Serve: Spoon the risotto onto plates, sprinkle the reserved mushrooms on top, and finish with a few drops of truffle pate (5g) for a classic finishing touch.

source_prompt: Three-bean vegetarian chili with roasted poblano, smoked paprika, dark chocolate for depth, and a lime crema. Cornbread on the side.
name: Three-Bean Vegetarian Chili with Roasted Poblano and Lime Crema
instructions: Preheat your oven to 200°C (400°F).

Chop the poblano peppers in half and remove the seeds. Place them skin-side up on a baking sheet. Roast in the preheated oven for about 20-25 minutes until the skins are blistered and blackened. Remove from the oven and place in a bowl covered with plastic wrap to steam for 10 minutes. This will make peeling easier.

While the peppers are roasting, prepare your chili base. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until the onions are translucent and the vegetables have softened, stirring occasionally, until fragrant.

Add the garlic (minced) to the pot and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Then, stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, thyme, salt, and black pepper. Allow these spices to bloom for about 1 minute.

Pour in the vegetable broth, bringing it to a simmer. Reduce heat to low and add the black beans and kidney beans. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chili to thicken slightly.

Peel the roasted poblano peppers, chop them into small pieces, and add to the chili pot. Stir in the dark chocolate, mixing until melted and well incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
While the chili is simmering, prepare the lime crema by mixing sour cream with lime juice, zesting if desired, and a pinch of salt. Adjust lime juice to taste; it should be tangy and bright.
Once the chili is ready, serve it hot, drizzling lime crema generously on top for an extra zing of flavor. Enjoy with cornbread on the side for a comforting and hearty meal.

source_prompt: Vegetable biryani with saffron-soaked rice, layered spiced vegetables, fried onions, mint, and a cooling cucumber raita.
name: Layered Vegetable Biryani with Cooling Cucumber Raita
instructions: Soak 1 gram of saffron in 2 tablespoons of warm water to release its color. Set aside while preparing the vegetables.
Heat 30 grams of vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Once hot, add 100 grams of finely sliced onions, sautéing until golden brown (about 5-7 minutes).
Add 150 grams of chopped cauliflower, 100 grams of chopped carrots, and 100 grams of peas to the pot. Cook for 4-5 minutes until vegetables start to soften, stirring occasionally.
Stir in 5 grams of ground turmeric, 5 grams of cumin seeds, and 5 grams of chili powder, sautéing for another 2 minutes to bloom the spices. The aroma will be fragrant and earthy.
Next, add enough water (about 1 liter) to the pot to cover the vegetables, and drop in one bay leaf for added flavor. Bring to a simmer.

In a separate pot, rinse 200 grams of basmati rice under cold water until the water runs clear to remove excess starch. Then, add it to the pot with the vegetables, along with the saffron mixture and a pinch of salt.
Cover the pot, reduce heat to low, and let it steam for about 20 minutes or until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid. Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving.
Meanwhile, prepare the cucumber raita: finely chop 150 grams of cucumber and mix with 200 grams of plain low-fat yogurt, 10 grams of fresh spearmint, and a pinch of salt. Chill until ready to serve.
Once the biryani is cooked, let it rest covered for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the flavors to meld.
To plate, gently layer the biryani onto a dish, top with extra mint leaves, and serve alongside the cooling cucumber raita for contrast in flavor. Enjoy!

source_prompt: 25-minute Thai-style chicken larb in cabbage cups — minced chicken with lime, fish sauce, toasted rice powder, mint and chili.
name: Zesty Thai Chicken Larb in Cabbage Cups
instructions: In a dry pan, toast 10g of coriander seeds over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant and golden, stirring frequently to ensure even browning. Remove and crush lightly. The aroma should be nutty and warm.

In the same pan, add 400g of ground chicken over medium-high heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, breaking it apart with a spoon until it turns golden brown and is fully cooked. It should no longer be pink and have a slightly crispy texture on the edges.
Add in 10g of minced shallots and 10g of minced garlic to the pan. Sauté for another 2-3 minutes until the shallots soften and turn translucent, releasing a sweet aroma.
Deglaze the pan with 30g of fish broth and scrape up any golden bits stuck to the bottom. Cook for an additional 2 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and the liquid to reduce slightly.

Squeeze in 50g of lime juice from the fresh limes and stir well. Add in the toasted coriander, 20g of finely chopped hot chili peppers, and 20g of fresh mint. Mix everything together, adjusting the seasoning with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Remove the chicken mixture from the heat and let cool slightly while you prepare the cabbage cups. Take 200g of cabbage leaves and gently separate them, allowing them to be used as cups for serving.
To assemble, spoon the chicken larb mixture into each cabbage cup. Top with additional mint and a drizzle of 10g of cider vinegar for tanginess.
Serve the larb immediately with extra lime wedges and rice crackers for crunch on the side. Enjoy the vibrant flavors and aroma that sing the essence of Thai cuisine.

source_prompt: 30-minute turkey and zucchini meatballs simmered in a quick marinara with basil, over spaghetti.
name: Savory Turkey and Zucchini Meatballs in Quick Marinara
instructions: **Prep Ingredients:** Finely chop 200g of zucchini, mince 10g of garlic, and dice 100g of onion.
**Mix Meatballs:** In a large bowl, combine 500g of ground turkey, chopped zucchini, minced garlic, and 5g of salt. Mix well until fully combined.
**Form Meatballs:** Roll the mixture into meatballs about the size of a golf ball (approximately 30g each). You should have around 8-10 meatballs.
**Heat Oil:** In a large skillet, heat 30g of olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering.
**Sear Meatballs:** Carefully place meatballs into the skillet. Sear for 5-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until all sides are golden brown and a crust forms.
**Add Aromatics:** Add the diced onions to the skillet. Sauté alongside the meatballs for about 3-4 minutes until onions are translucent and fragrant.
**Deglaze with Marinara:** Pour 300g of marinara sauce into the skillet, scraping the bottom of the pan to release any brown bits. Bring to a simmer.
**Simmer:** Reduce heat to medium-low and let simmer for 10-12 minutes, until the meatballs are cooked through. Stir occasionally.
**Cook Spaghetti:** While the meatballs simmer, cook 160g of spaghetti in salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente, about 8-10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
**Season Sauce:** Taste the marinara sauce and adjust seasoning with additional salt and 5g of black pepper, if desired.
**Serve:** Serve the meatballs and sauce over the cooked spaghetti. Top with 30g of grated Parmesan cheese and sprinkle with fresh basil before enjoying.

source_prompt: Slow-cooker pulled pork with a smoky BBQ sauce — sandwich filling that gets better through the week. Serve on brioche buns with slaw.
name: Smoky BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwiches
instructions: Prepare the Pork: Season 800g of ground pork with 15g of smoked paprika, 20g of salt, and 10g of black pepper, mixing thoroughly. Let it marinate for 30 minutes to absorb flavors.
Sear the Pork: Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and add 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Once hot, sear the marinated pork for 5-6 minutes until browned, stirring occasionally to create a fond.
Prepare Onions: Dice 200g of onions and add them to the skillet, cooking for 3-4 minutes until they become translucent. Stir frequently to ensure even cooking and prevent burning.
Deglaze: Pour 60g of cider vinegar into the skillet, scraping up the brown bits from the bottom. This will enhance the flavor of the meat.
Combine Ingredients: Transfer the pork and onion mixture into a slow cooker. Add 800g of pulled pork in barbecue sauce and 150g of finely chopped cabbage. Stir until well combined.
Cook: Set the slow cooker on low for 8 hours or high for 4 hours. The pork should be tender and easily shredded with a fork. The aroma will be rich and inviting as it cooks.
Prepare Slaw: Meanwhile, combine 100g of coleslaw with 30g of mayonnaise, 10g of red wine vinegar, and 5g of sugar in a bowl. Mix well and refrigerate until ready to serve.
Assemble Sandwich: Once the pork is done, shred it using two forks and mix it with the barbecue sauce in the slow cooker. Toast brioche buns lightly before serving.
Serve: Layer the pulled pork on the bottom half of the bun, top with a generous scoop of slaw, and add the bun's top half. Enjoy your Smoky BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwiches!

source_prompt: Hearty white bean and chorizo stew with smoked paprika, kale, and a sherry-vinegar finish. Crusty bread alongside. Meal-prep staple.
name: Hearty White Bean & Chorizo Stew with Kale and Smoked Paprika
instructions: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Add 30g of olive oil and heat until shimmering, about 1 minute.
Once the oil is hot, add 200g of chorizo, cooking until browned and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Stir occasionally to ensure even browning.
Add 100g of chopped onions and 10g of minced garlic to the pot. Sauté until the onions are translucent, about 5 minutes, and fragrant.
Next, stir in 100g of diced carrots and 100g of diced celery. Cook for another 3-4 minutes until the vegetables begin to soften.
Sprinkle in 5g of smoked paprika, 5g of salt, 2g of black pepper, and 2 whole bay leaves. Stir for about 1 minute until the spices are fragrant and well-blended into the vegetable mixture.
Pour in 800g of vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it cook uncovered for about 15 minutes, allowing the flavors to develop.
Add 150g of kale and 400g of drained chickpeas (or white beans if available) to the pot. Stir gently and cook for an additional 10 minutes, until the kale is wilted and tender.
Remove the pot from heat. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as desired. Allow to rest for 5 minutes before serving.

source_prompt: Greek pastitsio — baked tubular pasta layered with cinnamon-and-clove-spiced lamb ragu and a thick béchamel. Cuts into proper portions.
name: Cinnamon-Spiced Lamb Pastitsio
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a large skillet over medium-high heat, add 50g of salted butter. Wait until it melts and becomes bubbly.
Add 150g of finely chopped onions and sauté for about 5 minutes until they turn translucent and aromatic.
Stir in 30g of minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to brown the garlic.
Add 400g of ground lamb to the skillet, breaking it apart with a spatula. Sear for about 5-7 minutes until well browned.
Season the meat with 5g of ground cinnamon, 3g of ground cloves, 8g of salt, and 5g of black pepper. Stir to coat the meat evenly with the spices.

Pour in 160ml of sheep milk and toss in 2 bay leaves. Bring the mixture to a simmer and let it cook for 20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and slightly thicken the sauce. Remove bay leaves after cooking.
While the ragu is simmering, cook 300g of enriched tubular pasta in a large pot of salted water until al dente, approximately 7-9 minutes. Drain and set aside.

In the same pot, prepare the béchamel sauce by melting 50g of butter over medium heat. Whisk in 50g of all-purpose flour and cook for about 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until it forms a roux and lightly turns golden.

Gradually whisk in 500ml of sheep milk until smooth. Cook the sauce on low heat, stirring frequently, until it thickens, about 8 minutes. Stir in 2g of ground nutmeg and adjust seasoning if necessary with salt and pepper.
In a large baking dish, layer half of the pasta, then spread half of the lamb ragu over it. Add half of the béchamel, then repeat the layers, finishing with the remaining béchamel on top.
Sprinkle 50g of grated milk crackers on top for added texture and crunch. Bake in the preheated oven for 30-35 minutes until golden brown and bubbling.
Once done, let the pastitsio rest for about 10 minutes before slicing. Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
